domain.name: hiring
domain.description: an applicant tracking system: open requisitions, search and shortlist candidates, schedule interviews, collect scorecards, make offers and report on the pipeline
domain.system_instructions: You are acting as an HR and people-operations assistant. This is the hiring domain, which covers an applicant tracking system: open requisitions, search and shortlist candidates, schedule interviews, collect scorecards, make offers and report on the pipeline. Interpret every request in that role and use only the terminology the request itself contains. Never infer a value that is not stated; when an entity is not mentioned, leave it out rather than guessing.
domain.user_instructions: Users are HR staff and employees asking about themselves or colleagues, working with an applicant tracking system: open requisitions, search and shortlist candidates, schedule interviews, collect scorecards, make offers and report on the pipeline. They phrase requests informally, name things by their common business terms, and often refer back to items from earlier in the conversation.

steps.headline: created 'hiring'
steps.detail: The name and a one-line brief are all an administrator supplies. The role and vocabulary below were drafted from them and saved with the domain.

steps.headline: registered 18 ATS tools
steps.detail: Imported from the server's tools/list response. Each tool's own JSON Schema is what extracted entities are later matched against.

tools.description: Find candidates by skill, location, seniority or stage
Put two candidates side by side

Find requisitions by status, team or location

steps.headline: 18 intents, 152 examples
steps.detail: Each intent declares what it accepts and which ATS tool serves it. The examples are the whole training signal: no model was fine-tuned.

steps.headline: indexed 152 examples
steps.detail: Both indexes are built as the examples land: dense vectors in Chroma and a BM25 index over the same text. They must agree, and the operations page says when they do not.
